_comment: 2026-08-27 (latest): macOS 5.0.2 build 388 UPLOADED, awaiting review. app_store still 5.0.
What is live on the App Store, versus what is being prepared.
This file exists because the three public websites had no way to tell those apart.
CHANGELOG.md's first numbered heading is the release being PREPARED, not the one that
shipped: ci_post_clone.sh reads it to stamp MARKETING_VERSION for the build. Gunzino's
version workflow read that same heading and labelled it 'Shipped version', so on
2026-08-13 gunzino.me advertised 5.0 while App Store Connect download data showed 4.9 as
the newest version any user had. Docs/ai/STATE.md and the RepoOS router made the same
conflation.
Update app_store when a build actually goes live, not when it is submitted.
Update preparing when a new numbered heading is added to CHANGELOG.md.
Both values must match a '## <version>' heading in CHANGELOG.md; the sync workflows fail
loudly if they do not, rather than publishing a guess.
2026-08-27 (later): macOS 5.0.1 is APPROVED AND LIVE, so in_review is now empty and
app_store_by_platform.macos is 5.0.1. app_store DELIBERATELY STAYS AT 5.0. The prior
ACTION note said to set app_store to 5.0.1, but its own next sentence says not to move it
past what iOS actually has, and iOS is still on 5.0. The platforms have simply swapped
roles: macOS now leads, iOS lags. The rule this file was created to enforce is to publish
the value that does not overclaim to a visitor on the lagging platform, so 5.0 it is.
Revisit when iOS reaches 5.0.1 or later.
macOS 5.0.2 is being prepared: it is the first release where a Mac user can get a document
into the app at all. Both the Add Documents button and Finder drag-and-drop were broken or
absent in 5.0 and 5.0.1.
2026-08-27: iOS 5.0 approved. Both platforms were live at 5.0 as of this date.
2026-08-26: the two platforms diverged, which this schema cannot express in one number.
macOS 5.0 (build 379) is APPROVED AND LIVE. iOS 5.0 (build 386) is IN REVIEW, so the
newest version an iPhone or iPad user can install is still 4.9. app_store therefore stays
at 4.9 on purpose: it is the value that does not overclaim to an iOS visitor, and
understating is the safe direction for the exact failure this file was created to stop.
verified_against: macOS 5.0.2 (build 388) uploaded to App Store Connect 2026-08-27 via the App Store Upload workflow, run 33124470371; all gates passed including the prerelease build-machine-stamp check. macOS 5.0.1 live since 2026-08-27. iOS 5.0 (build 386) live; iOS remains the lagging platform, so app_store stays at 5.0.
